source_location: Paper p. 5, Part III; model_results.json assumptions.population
source_text: The public-finance exercise follows one million people from age 60 until the chosen retirement age.
social_wording: The model follows a one-million-person cohort from age 60.
qualifier: Scenario cohort; South Africa context; not a population forecast

source_location: Paper p. 3, Part I table; p. 8, Figure 2; model_results.json policies.average
source_text: Compared with retirement at 60, the average scenario produces cumulative public gains of R213bn at 65, R369bn at 70 and R448bn at 75.
social_wording: Average-case cumulative public gain: R213bn at 65, R369bn at 70 and R448bn at 75.
qualifier: Constant 2026 rand; cumulative; undiscounted; one million people; not a forecast

source_text: In the average case, the first five-year delay produces R213bn, the next adds R156bn and the final five adds R79bn.
social_wording: The incremental fiscal gain shrinks from R213bn to R156bn to R79bn across successive five-year shifts.
qualifier: Constant 2026 rand; cumulative; undiscounted; average scenario; versus retirement at 60

source_location: Paper p. 7, Part V table; model_results.json policies.average
source_text: The average scenario produces 0.74m unsupported bridge-years at 65, 2.05m at 70 and 3.99m at 75.
social_wording: At age 75, the model produces 3.99m unsupported bridge-years.
qualifier: Modeled years; potentially grant-eligible people; household support outside the model is not tracked

source_location: Paper p. 3, Part I table; model_results.json policies.average
source_text: The average scenario produces 0.27m disability claim-years at 65, 0.81m at 70 and 1.61m at 75.
social_wording: At age 75, the model produces 1.61m disability claim-years.
qualifier: Modeled claim-years; one-million-person cohort; not a clinical forecast

source_location: Paper p. 10, Part VIII; Figure 4; model_results.json policies
source_text: At age 70, the expansion case adds 0.32m youth job-years, the average case removes 0.79m and the worst case removes 2.16m.
social_wording: At age 70, youth job-years range from +0.32m to -2.16m across the three labour-market scenarios.
qualifier: Imposed complementarity or displacement assumptions; not a causal estimate

source_location: Paper p. 3, Part I; p. 14, Part XII
source_text: Age 65 looks fiscally robust in all three cases; age 70 needs better job matching and disability protection; age 75 faces a higher evidence threshold.
social_wording: Age 65 is fiscally robust across the modeled cases; 70 is conditional; 75 needs stronger evidence.
qualifier: Policy interpretation of scenario results, not a universal retirement-age recommendation

source_text: This is an armchair scenario model, not actuarial advice, a forecast or a causal estimate. Money values are constant 2026 rand; fiscal and output totals are cumulative and undiscounted.
social_wording: These are cumulative, undiscounted scenario results in constant 2026 rand - not a forecast.
qualifier: Armchair scenario model; policy ages are experiments

source_location: Paper p. 7, Part V; p. 9, Part VII
source_text: A legal age does not create a suitable job or restore health; a narrow fiscal gain can shift costs to households during unsupported bridge years.
social_wording: The budget can gain while bridge-year risk shifts to households.
qualifier: Interpretation governed by modeled employment, disability and unsupported bridge-year assumptions
